newsitem.title: USA: United Petroleum begins holder value study.
newsitem.headline: United Petroleum begins holder value study.

text.p: United Petroleum Corp said Wednesday it has begun a study aimed at maximizing shareholder value.

The effort, initiated by directors in response to the recent decline in the company's stock, will review all aspects of the company including its operating structure, capital structure, operating performance, debt terms and nature, and organizational structure, United said.
The results of the board's recommendations are expected to be announced over the next few weeks and months, with some actions expected near-term, the company said.
United also said its core businesses remain strong, and that no broad change in the nature of the company's businesses is expected at this time.
The company said the study's results will include specific recommendations for changes in structure and operations.
It said the study will also look at implementation of Economic Value Added measurement techniques as part of the company's management objective and compensation process.

"While artificial factors, including certain market activity such as shorting, that are beyond the company's control, may be a significant influence on our current valuation, we nevertheless recognize a need to continue to improve the quality and value of our business," the company's statement explained.

Although mentioning such specific actions as one-time dividends, spinoffs or a financial restructuring as being under consideration, it said: "We are examining all options, both structurally and operationally. If repositioning the company, or its structure, would improve our ability to succeed, and thus increase the potential shareholder value, it will be evaluated thoroughly."
